name: hamming
description: A parameterizable Hsiao single-error-correcting, double-error-detecting (SEC-DED) codec: an encoder that appends PW check bits to a DW-bit word and a decoder that corrects any single-bit error and detects any double-bit error.
authorship: Zero ASIC Corporation; author Andreas Olofsson

human_review.notes: Provenance (model and date) confirmed by the author; architecture, scope, and verification were directed and reviewed by the author.

spec.summary: Synthesizable, parameterizable Hsiao SEC-DED codec. The encoder hamming_enc appends PW check bits to a DW-bit data word to form a DW+PW-bit systematic codeword, computing each check bit as a constant-folded XOR tree over the data. The decoder hamming_dec recomputes the syndrome, compares it against the constant column table, corrects the matching single-bit error, and outputs the DW-bit corrected data plus the PW-bit syndrome. The parity-check matrix is H = [ M | I_PW ], where data bit k owns the k-th distinct odd-weight, weight>=3 PW-bit column taken lightest-weight first. The benchmark top hamming wires the encoder codeword into the decoder through an error-injection XOR (err_mask) so the round-trip can exercise correction and detection. Because every column is odd weight, single-bit errors map to odd-weight syndromes and double errors to even-weight syndromes. The construction is the standard ECC used on memory and data paths.
key_decisions: Use the Hsiao minimum odd-weight-column SEC-DED construction (H = [ M | I_PW ], identity check block) so single errors give odd-weight syndromes, double errors give even-weight syndromes, and parity-tree fan-in is balanced.

Assign data columns lightest-weight first (all weight-3 columns, then weight-5, ...) and require PW large enough that the count of odd-weight weight>=3 columns is at least DW (DW=64 needs PW=8: 56 weight-3 plus 8 weight-5).

Build the column table once in an always @* block via popcount and weight-ordered fill, with no Verilog functions, so the entire table folds to constants at synthesis and each check bit becomes a fixed XOR of data bits.
Keep encoder and decoder on the identical column assignment, guarded by the round-trip smoke test, so syndrome equality compares match the encoder's parity tree.
Expose PIPELINE so the codec is either purely combinational (PIPELINE=0) or registers the input for a one-cycle path (PIPELINE=1) using clk and async active-low nreset.
Map to LUTs only (plus FFs when pipelined): combinational XOR parity trees, syndrome equality compares, and correction XORs; no DSP and no BRAM.

origin.notes: Original implementation written for LogikBench; follows the cited algorithm/standard and hardware architectures, not copied from any specific HDL source.

references: R. W. Hamming, 'Error detecting and error correcting codes,' Bell System Technical Journal, vol. 29, no. 2, pp. 147-160, Apr. 1950.
M. Y. Hsiao, 'A class of optimal minimum odd-weight-column SEC-DED codes,' IBM Journal of Research and Development, vol. 14, no. 4, pp. 395-401, Jul. 1970.
S. Lin and D. J. Costello, Error Control Coding, 2nd ed., Prentice Hall, 2004.
C. L. Chen and M. Y. Hsiao, 'Error-correcting codes for semiconductor memory applications: A state-of-the-art review,' IBM Journal of Research and Development, vol. 28, no. 2, pp. 124-134, Mar. 1984.
